Welcome to Churcham Primary School
“Pupils learn together and respect one another within and beyond the classroom.” – Ofsted, January 2024
It gives me great pleasure to welcome you to our website and to thank you for taking the time to visit us.
Churcham Primary School has been serving its community since 1850, and we are immensely proud of our long history. Today, our school has two classes:
Class 1 – Reception, Year 1 and Year 2
Class 2 – Years 3, 4, 5 and 6
You can find out more about life in each class on their dedicated pages.
Churcham is a happy, friendly school, and I consider it an absolute privilege to be its Headteacher. Our vision — learning, respecting and growing together as a whole school family — captures the relationships, values and sense of belonging that shape daily life here. We believe that, regardless of age, everyone has something to contribute and something to learn.
We hope you enjoy exploring our website. Of course, this is only a glimpse into our wonderful school. We would be delighted to welcome you in person and show you what makes Churcham such a special place to learn.
Please contact us if you would like to arrange a visit or if you have any questions.

British Values

British Values
The Department for Education has published guidance on promoting fundamental British values in schools. At Churcham Primary School, we see this as a duty to ensure that our children are prepared for a successful life as British Citizens.
At Churcham Primary School we uphold and teach pupils about British Values which are defined as:
Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and Beliefs
These values are taught explicitly through Personal, Social, Health and Emotional (PSHE), and Religious Education (RE). We also teach British Values through planning and delivering a broad and balanced curriculum. Our termly values are also central to our approach.
The school takes opportunities to actively promote British Values through daily reflections and whole school systems and structures such as electing and running a successful School Council. We also actively promote British Values through ensuring that our curriculum planning and delivery includes real opportunities for exploring these values.
Democracy:
The school council is elected through a democratic process using class pupil votes. During these elections, pupils are provided with the opportunity to learn how to argue and defend their point of view. The school council gives every pupil a voice and the chance to be involved in a range of decision-making opportunities throughout the school.
Throughout the curriculum, children are given opportunities to debate their ideas and thoughts and to use voting when making class decisions. This supports pupils to understand how citizens can influence decision-making through the democratic process.
The Rule of Law:
The school rules are embedded into the values of both schools. Pupils understand that the rules keep them safe and enable them to learn through a fair and consistent approach which ensures they successfully live and work together.
Pupils are taught the value and reasons behind laws, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken. Visits from a variety of authorities help reinforce this message.
To encourage and promote good behaviour, attitude and work, we have devised a behaviour system which is consistently followed throughout the school. We are committed to praising children's efforts. We endeavour to praise the children informally, individually, during group work, in front of the whole class and school assemblies. Children are rewarded not only for achievement in curriculum areas, but also for behaviour and demonstration of values. Rewards are given in the form of stickers, table and house points and certificates. Children's achievements are also recognised during assemblies and highlighted in our special book.
Individual Liberty:
Through our curriculum, our PSHE lessons and through our assemblies, children are supported to understand their personal rights and freedoms. Pupils are actively encouraged to make choices at our school, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. Children are encouraged to raise ideas and to contribute to the life of the school.
Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and are advised how to exercise these safely, for example through our E-Safety teaching and PHSE education.
Churcham Primary School has a robust anti-bullying culture and has in place a comprehensive Behaviour Policy, which has at its heart the freedom for all students to learn and grow safely.
Mutual Respect:
Respect underpins all that we do at Churcham. It is truly embedded into the curriculum and the ethos of the schools. We insist that all pupils, teachers, non-teaching staff and visitors to our school are treated with dignity and respect. This is expressed by all demonstrating good manners and fostering positive and professional relationships. Pupils learn that their behaviours have an effect on their own rights and those of others. All members of the school community treat each other with courtesy and respect and these values underpin all teaching and learning and all relationships in our school.
Tolerance of Those of Different Faiths and Beliefs:
At Churcham Primary School, we are committed to ensuring that our children understand the cultures, faiths and beliefs of their friends, neighbours and the communities beyond our schools.
We promote that all children visit a range of places of worship and learn about different religious beliefs in our religious education lessons and assemblies. Beliefs, traditions and customs are studied and celebrated, reinforcing a deep understanding of British tolerance and acceptance of all cultures. We have a rich programme of language teaching and Language Days are built into our school calendar.
At Churcham Primary School, we will actively challenge pupils, staff or parents expressing opinions contrary to fundamental British Values, including 'extremist' views.

Modern Foreign Languages (MFL)
Modern Foreign Languages (MFL) at Churcham
Our Vision for Language Learning at Churcham
At Churcham Primary School, we believe that learning a foreign language opens doors to the wider world. Through French, pupils develop communication skills, cultural awareness and a deeper understanding of themselves and others. Our curriculum is designed to spark curiosity, build confidence and inspire a lifelong enthusiasm for language learning.
We want every child to feel capable, motivated and excited about exploring new languages and cultures — preparing them for future opportunities in education, travel and work.
INTENT
Our MFL curriculum aims to equip pupils with the skills, knowledge and confidence to communicate in French and appreciate cultural diversity.
We aim for pupils to:
Receive four years of structured French education across KS2
Develop strong listening, speaking, reading and writing skills
Understand and apply key vocabulary and grammatical structures
Build phonetic awareness through Physical French Phonics
Gain confidence expressing ideas, emotions and opinions in French
Appreciate French culture and develop intercultural understanding
Become motivated, independent language learners
We use Language Angels alongside Physical French Phonics to deliver a rich, engaging and ambitious curriculum that supports progression, enjoyment and high‑quality learning.
IMPLEMENTATION
French is taught weekly across Key Stage Two in mixed‑age classes (Years 3–6). Lessons are delivered by class teachers using the Language Angels scheme and Physical French Phonics, ensuring consistency, progression and strong phonics foundations.
Curriculum Design
The Language Angels curriculum map is tailored specifically for Churcham, ensuring progression in vocabulary, grammar and phonics.
Themes and topics build on prior learning and deepen understanding year by year.
Pupils hear native French speakers via online resources to strengthen listening and pronunciation.
Teaching Approaches
French lessons are dynamic, enjoyable and interactive. They include:
Physical actions for key sounds and phrases
Digital tools (iPads, laptops) for recording spoken and written work
Opportunities to practise everyday expressions such as merci and excusez‑moi
Intercultural Awareness
Pupils explore French customs, traditions and cultural practices. Special events — such as the European Day of Languages — provide focused cultural learning and celebration.
Families are invited to share their own language knowledge, strengthening community engagement and cultural appreciation.
Cross‑Curricular Links
Where possible, French learning connects with other subjects, enriching pupils’ wider understanding and supporting retention.
Celebrating Learning
Displayed in classrooms
Shared in assemblies
Posted on Class Dojo
Celebrated during themed events
This visibility reinforces language learning across the school environment.
IMPACT
The effectiveness of our MFL curriculum is monitored through a combination of formative and summative assessment, pupil voice and visible language use across school.
Assessment
Learning outcomes are recorded in French exercise books and digitally via iPads.
Teachers use weekly lessons for ongoing formative assessment, adjusting pacing and support as needed.
Pupils reflect on their own understanding and choose tasks suited to their confidence level.
Summative assessments take place each half term using foundation subject criteria.
Pupil Voice
Annual pupil voice sessions provide valuable insight into engagement, enjoyment and cultural understanding.
Language Presence Across School
Incidental French used by staff and pupils
Cultural event displays
Regular updates to parents via newsletters and Class Dojo
Outcomes
By the end of KS2, pupils:
Communicate confidently in French
Understand key phonics, vocabulary and grammar
Demonstrate strong listening and pronunciation skills
Appreciate cultural diversity
Are equipped with strategies for future language learning
Why MFL Matters at Churcham
Learning French helps pupils:
Build communication skills
Develop cultural awareness and empathy
Strengthen memory and cognitive flexibility
Gain confidence expressing themselves
Prepare for future opportunities in a global world
Enjoy discovering new languages and cultures
Our curriculum ensures every child becomes a confident, curious and capable language learner.

Special Educational Needs (SEND)
Special Educational Needs and Disability at Churcham
Special Educational Needs & Disabilities (SEND)
At Churcham Primary School, we are committed to ensuring every child can thrive, achieve and feel valued. Some children may need additional support at different points in their school journey. Our approach to SEND is rooted in early identification, strong partnerships with families, and high‑quality inclusive teaching.
We follow the SEND Code of Practice (2015) and work closely with Gloucestershire County Council to ensure our provision meets the needs of all learners.
Our SENDCo
Our Special Educational Needs & Disabilities Coordinator (SENDCo) is:
Miss Richelle Daniels Email: [email protected]
Miss Daniels oversees SEND provision across the school, ensuring our practice is consistent with national guidance, the Local Offer, and our own school policies. She works closely with pupils, families, staff and external professionals to ensure every child receives the right support at the right time.
Our SEND Provision
We support children with needs in the following broad areas:
Communication and Interaction (e.g., speech, language and communication needs; autism spectrum conditions)
Cognition and Learning (e.g., difficulties with memory, processing, literacy or numeracy)
Social, Emotional and Mental Health (e.g., anxiety, emotional regulation, behaviour needs)
Sensory and/or Physical Needs (e.g., hearing or visual impairment, physical disabilities, medical needs)
Our provision is based on the Graduated Response:Assess → Plan → Do → Review, ensuring support is tailored, monitored and regularly reviewed with families.
Working With Families
We believe that strong relationships with parents and carers are essential. We:
listen carefully to concerns
involve families in decision‑making
share targets and strategies
review progress together
signpost external support when needed
Children’s voices are central to our SEND practice. We encourage pupils to share their views, celebrate their strengths and help shape their own support.
Gloucestershire Local Offer
You can find out more about SEND support across Gloucestershire, including services, guidance and pathways, through the Local Offer:
Gloucestershire Local Offer: Glosfamilies Directory | Support for Families with SEND - Gloucestershire's Local Offer for Parent Carers
Our SEND Documents
You can access our SEND policies and information below:
Accessibility Plan 2026
SEND Statement of Intent
DfE Guidance on SEND for Parents
If You Have Concerns About Your Child
If you are worried about your child’s learning, development or wellbeing, please speak to your child’s class teacher or contact Miss Daniels directly. Early conversations help us put the right support in place quickly.

Art and Design and Technology (D+T)
Art and Design and Technology (D+T) at Churcham
Art & Design and Design & Technology at Churcham Primary School
Learning, respecting and growing together as a whole school family
Our Vision for Creativity at Churcham
At Churcham Primary School, creativity is at the heart of our curriculum. Through Art & Design and Design & Technology (DT), pupils develop the confidence to explore, experiment, innovate and express themselves. Both subjects are taught through carefully sequenced, high‑quality lessons that nurture curiosity, resilience and reflective thinking.
Our approach ensures that every child — including those with SEND or from disadvantaged backgrounds — is supported to thrive, feel valued, and grow as a creative individual.
ART & DESIGN
Intent
We believe that “every child is an artist” and that artistic expression is a powerful tool for personal development.
Our Art curriculum aims to ensure pupils:
Develop artistic skills across a wide range of mediums
Think critically by analysing and critiquing artworks
Appreciate diverse artistic traditions, cultures and perspectives
Express themselves creatively and emotionally
Build resilience, confidence and curiosity through high‑quality teaching
Every child’s creative journey is nurtured and celebrated — because confident artists come in many forms.
Implementation
Art is taught weekly for three terms of the year, alternating with DT, using our adapted Kapow Primary scheme. Lessons are practical, exploratory and hands‑on, with pupils using sketchbooks, mixed media and a wide range of materials.
Key features include:
Knowledge organisers to support vocabulary, recall and key concepts
Kapow specialist videos to model techniques
CPD videos for staff to strengthen subject knowledge
Cross‑curricular links (e.g., ratio in maths when mixing colours, imagination in English storytelling, artists linked to history topics)
Spiral curriculum revisiting skills with increasing complexity
Adaptive teaching including Widgit resources, pre‑teaching, chunked instruction, peer support and modelling
Non‑negotiables such as high‑quality terminology, self‑assessment, formative feedback and exposure to diverse artists
Impact
Our Art curriculum ensures pupils can confidently discuss their learning, evaluate their work and understand how to improve.
Impact is monitored through:
Lesson drop‑ins and observations
Summative assessment spreadsheets tracking ARE and GDS
By the end of KS2, pupils leave Churcham equipped with strong artistic foundations, creativity and confidence.
DESIGN & TECHNOLOGY
Intent
We believe that “every child is capable of being a designer through passion, exploration and the guidance of motivated teachers who model creativity and curiosity.”
DT at Churcham develops pupils as innovative thinkers who can design, make and evaluate with purpose. Our curriculum ensures pupils:
Take risks through drafting, modelling and testing
Think critically by analysing their own work and the work of others
Understand the impact of design and technology on everyday life
Become resourceful, resilient and reflective
Build confidence through real‑world, meaningful projects
Every child’s DT journey is nurtured and celebrated — because confident designers come in many forms.
Implementation
DT is taught weekly for three terms of the year, alternating with Art, using our adapted Kapow Primary scheme. Lessons follow the design cycle of ideation → creation → evaluation, ensuring consistency and progression.
Key features include:
Hands‑on, practical learning including independent, paired and group tasks
Knowledge organisers to support recall and vocabulary
Kapow specialist videos modelling techniques
CPD videos for staff
Cross‑curricular links (e.g., measuring in maths, materials in science, creativity in art)
Cooking & nutrition taught as a dedicated strand focusing on diet, seasonality and food origins
Spiral curriculum revisiting design processes with increasing complexity
Adaptive teaching including Widgit resources, chunked instruction, pre‑teaching, modelling and targeted support
Non‑negotiables such as high‑quality terminology, self‑assessment, formative feedback and consistent modelling
Impact
Our DT curriculum ensures pupils can evaluate their outcomes, articulate their design choices and understand how to improve.
Impact is monitored through:
Lesson drop‑ins and observations
Summative assessment spreadsheets tracking ARE and GDS
By the end of KS2, pupils leave Churcham equipped with a strong foundation of techniques, creativity and confidence to continue their DT learning beyond primary school.
Why Art & DT Matter at Churcham:
Together, Art and DT provide pupils with:
Opportunities to express themselves
Skills to solve problems creatively
Confidence to take risks
Resilience through iterative improvement
Cultural and real‑world understanding
A sense of pride in their creations
These subjects play a vital role in developing well‑rounded, reflective and imaginative learners.

Our Sports Premium Grant report can be found below:
Physical Education at Churcham Primary School
We deliver our high‑quality, fully‑adapted PE curriculum using the GetSet4PE scheme. Teachers plan and adapt lessons to ensure all pupils, including those with SEND, can participate, progress and enjoy physical activity across the year.
Swimming and Water Safety
Swimming is a statutory part of the National Curriculum, and all schools must provide swimming instruction in either Key Stage 1 or Key Stage 2. At Churcham, we teach swimming in Years 3, 4 and 5 during the Spring term. Depending on the length of the term, pupils receive 10–12 lessons, each lasting 45 minutes.
In line with the National Curriculum (2014), pupils are taught to:
swim competently, confidently and proficiently over a distance of at least 25 metres
use a range of strokes effectively (for example, front crawl, backstroke and breaststroke)
perform safe self‑rescue in different water‑based situations

PSHE/RSE
Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education and Relationships and Sex Education at Churcham
Learning, respecting and growing together as a whole school family
“Understanding myself and others”
Our Vision for Personal, Social, Health & Relationships Education
At Churcham Primary School, PSHE and RSE are central to developing confident, emotionally intelligent and responsible young citizens. Our curriculum supports pupils to understand themselves, build healthy relationships, stay safe and thrive within their community.
We believe every child deserves the knowledge, skills and strategies to navigate modern life with resilience, empathy and self‑belief. Through high‑quality teaching and a nurturing environment, we help pupils grow into thoughtful, respectful and independent individuals.
INTENT
Our PSHE/RSE curriculum is designed to equip pupils with the essential skills needed to become healthy, independent and responsible members of society.
We aim for pupils to:
Understand and manage their emotions
Build and maintain positive relationships
Develop resilience, empathy and self‑worth
Stay safe and make informed choices
Communicate respectfully and confidently
Contribute positively to their community
Our programme of study — SCARF (Safety, Caring, Achievement, Resilience, Friendship) — supports whole‑child development through carefully planned, resourced and progressive lessons.
By the time pupils leave Churcham, they will have the emotional intelligence, wellbeing strategies and confidence needed to flourish in modern life.
IMPLEMENTATION
PSHE/RSE is taught weekly across the whole school using a consistent, progressive approach. Our curriculum includes all statutory Relationships and Health Education content and is organised into a four‑year rolling programme to ensure full coverage without repetition.
Our Six Half‑Termly Themes
Me and My Relationships – healthy relationships, communication, conflict resolution
Valuing Differences – diversity, inclusion, anti‑bullying
Keeping Safe – recognising risks, knowing who and where is safe
Rights and Respect – personal responsibility, community roles, financial awareness
Being My Best – achievements, self‑esteem, aspirations
Growing and Changing – age‑appropriate RSE, managing change positively
How Learning Happens
We use a wide range of teaching tools to ensure accessibility for all pupils, including:
Videos and visual stimuli
Structured discussions
SCARF resources and materials
Recording Learning
EYFS & KS1: pupils use a PSHE folder to collect significant learning (drawings, writing, reflections).
KS2: pupils record learning in a PSHE exercise book (brainstorms, letters, opinions, worksheets).
Teaching & Learning You Will See Across School
Quality first teaching adapted for all learners
Respectful, safe learning environments where every voice is valued
High‑quality questioning to deepen thinking
Opportunities to explore themes in depth
Circle time routines to support listening, sharing and emotional safety
SEND & Disadvantaged Support
Our PSHE/RSE curriculum is fully adaptable to ensure all pupils can access learning safely and meaningfully.
Adaptations include:
Pre‑teaching vocabulary
Adjusted SCARF resources
Sensitive content checks
Structured discussion routines
Non‑Negotiables
Clear rules to ensure all pupils feel listened to
Safe, respectful and inclusive environment
Accessible resources for all learners
Opportunities for discussion where every child is heard
IMPACT
The impact of our PSHE/RSE curriculum is monitored through:
KS1 folders and KS2 exercise books
Lesson observations and drop‑ins
By the end of KS2, pupils will be:
Healthy, open‑minded and respectful
Emotionally intelligent and resilient
Responsible citizens who value diversity
Confident in expressing themselves and supporting others
Why PSHE & RSE Matter at Churcham
PSHE/RSE helps pupils:
Understand themselves and others
Build healthy relationships
Make safe and informed choices
Develop empathy and emotional literacy
Grow confidence and self‑worth
Become active, responsible citizens
Our curriculum ensures every child is supported to flourish socially, emotionally and personally.

Governors
The Governing Body warmly welcomes you to the Churcham Primary School website.
Our governors work hard to support the Headteacher, staff and pupils, ensuring that Churcham Primary School provides the best possible education and prepares children for life in modern Britain. School governors are volunteers who want to make a positive difference to children’s education. Together with the Headteacher, they help set the strategic direction of the school, oversee the use of the school’s budget and make collective decisions on key matters such as policies and the school development plan. Governors also act as a critical friend, offering both support and challenge.
Members of the Governing Body are appointed by the local authority, the community and parents. All our governors bring a wide range of skills and experience from their own careers and responsibilities. Some are able to visit the school regularly, while others contribute financial, legal, strategic or practical expertise. Every governor is valued for the commitment they bring to our school.
Alongside their shared desire to support Churcham, governors also have statutory duties. They are legally responsible for areas including teaching and learning, safeguarding, health and safety, staffing, premises, and ensuring financial accountability and sustainability. The full Governing Body meets once every term, and two committees meet regularly to focus on specific areas of school leadership:
Teaching & Learning Committee
Resources Committee – Remit
The Resources Committee is responsible for overseeing the school’s financial management, staffing, premises and health & safety. Its remit includes:
monitoring and approving the school budget
ensuring financial probity and compliance with the Schools Financial Value Standard (SFVS)
overseeing staffing structure, recruitment and HR matters
monitoring the impact and sustainability of staffing decisions
overseeing premises, site security and health & safety compliance
ensuring statutory policies relating to finance, HR and premises are reviewed and up to date
monitoring risk management and ensuring appropriate controls are in place
This committee ensures the school uses its resources efficiently, safely and in the best interests of pupils.
Teaching & Learning Committee – Remit
The Teaching & Learning Committee is responsible for monitoring the quality of education, pupil outcomes and safeguarding. Its remit includes:
monitoring the curriculum, teaching quality and learning provision
reviewing pupil progress and attainment across all groups
ensuring the school meets statutory curriculum requirements
overseeing SEND provision and inclusion
monitoring safeguarding arrangements and compliance with Keeping Children Safe in Education
reviewing behaviour, attendance and personal development
ensuring statutory policies relating to teaching, learning, safeguarding and inclusion are reviewed and up to date
monitoring the impact of school improvement priorities
This committee ensures the school provides a high‑quality, safe and inclusive education for all pupils.
Full Governing Body
The Full Governing Body:
sets the school’s strategic direction
approves key policies
monitors overall performance
ensures statutory duties are met
holds the Headteacher to account for educational and safeguarding outcomes
ensures financial and resource decisions support the school’s priorities
If you have any concerns or matters you would like to discuss, please contact the Chair of Governors or any member of the Governing Body.

Music
Music at Churcham
Learning, respecting and growing together as a whole school family
“Where words fail, music speaks”
Our Vision for Music at Churcham
Music is a powerful form of expression, creativity and connection. At Churcham Primary School, we believe every child should experience the joy, discipline and inspiration that music brings. Through a rich and varied curriculum, pupils learn to listen, perform, compose and appreciate music from a wide range of genres and cultures.
We aim to nurture curiosity, confidence and creativity, helping pupils understand the value of music in their own lives and in the wider community. Music enriches personal development, strengthens emotional wellbeing and builds skills such as teamwork, resilience and self‑reflection.
INTENT
Our Music curriculum ensures pupils develop a secure understanding of what music is through listening, singing, playing, evaluating, analysing and composing. Children explore music across diverse genres, gaining knowledge of how music is created, produced and communicated.
We aim for pupils to:
Perform, listen to, review and evaluate music
Sing, create and compose using a range of techniques
Understand musical elements such as pitch, rhythm, dynamics and tempo
Use musical vocabulary confidently
Appreciate music from different cultures, traditions and historical periods
Develop creativity, self‑expression and confidence
Recognise the importance of music in the wider community
We are committed to fostering an unbiased respect for all types of music and supporting pupils to use their musical skills and experiences in a variety of contexts.
IMPLEMENTATION
Music is taught through the structured Charanga programme, ensuring progression, consistency and high‑quality teaching. This is complemented by weekly singing assemblies, concerts, performances and instrumental teaching delivered by specialist music teachers.
Curriculum Features
Singing, listening, playing, performing and evaluating embedded throughout lessons
Musical elements taught explicitly to support analysis and understanding
Opportunities to compose using instruments, body percussion and vocal sounds
Cross‑curricular links woven into lessons to deepen understanding
Exposure to a wide range of genres, styles and instruments
Teaching & Learning You Will See Across School
Teachers modelling new learning clearly and confidently
Quality first teaching adapted to meet the needs of all learners
Motivated pupils working within a “can‑do” musical environment
High‑quality questioning to deepen understanding
Misconceptions used to strengthen conceptual grasp
Carefully planned opportunities to explore, create and perform
SEND & Disadvantaged Support
Our Music curriculum is designed to be fully inclusive. Adaptations ensure all pupils can access learning, including:
Rephrased information
Tailored resources (including Widgit vocabulary)
Pre‑teaching of skills and vocabulary
Peer support and targeted adult support
Demonstrations and modelling
Visual aids and manipulatives
Opportunities to revisit and consolidate learning
Manipulatives & Resources
Charanga digital resources
A range of tuned and untuned instruments (string, percussion, etc.)
iPad and laptop applications
Word mats and vocabulary supports
Non‑Negotiables
Charanga used consistently as the structured scheme
High‑quality musical terminology used and understood
Pupils exposed to a wide range of instruments and genres
Adults model the use of manipulatives linked to learning objectives
IMPACT
Our varied and engaging curriculum enables pupils to discover strengths, identify areas for development and build confidence as musicians. Music supports achievement, self‑confidence, interaction and self‑reflection, enriching pupils’ personal development.
Over time, pupils develop knowledge across musical elements, gaining the ability to:
Sing with confidence and feel a pulse
Play tuned and untuned percussion instruments
Name and describe instruments and how they are played
Dissect music and understand its parts
Improvise and compose
Evaluate their own performance and that of others
Live performances and recordings showcase pupils’ creativity and progress. Assessment systems track progression in musical skills and knowledge.
Subject Leadership
Provides ongoing CPD to ensure high‑quality teaching
Gathers evidence from small‑group instrumental lessons
Collects pupil voice to evaluate enjoyment, understanding and confidence
Pupil voice demonstrates:
Enthusiasm and enjoyment when discussing music
Knowledge of musical styles and vocabulary
Confidence performing songs in groups
Understanding of improvisation vs. composition
Experience playing a range of percussion instruments
Why Music Matters at Churcham
Express themselves creatively
Build confidence and resilience
Develop listening and analytical skills
Appreciate cultural diversity
Work collaboratively
Experience joy through performance and creativity
Our curriculum ensures every child becomes a confident, curious and capable musician.

Science
Science at Churcham
Learning, respecting and growing together as a whole school family
“Wondering why”
Our Vision for Science at Churcham
At Churcham Primary School, Science is taught as a subject that inspires curiosity, deep thinking and a love of discovery. Our curriculum is designed to help pupils understand the world around them through hands‑on investigation, high‑quality teaching and rich scientific discussion.
We want every child to feel confident, valued and capable of becoming a scientist — one who asks questions, explores ideas and seeks to understand why things happen.
INTENT
Our Science curriculum is crafted to ignite curiosity and develop strong scientific enquiry skills. As stated in our curriculum document, “We thrive to nurture our children to be well‑versed in scientific vocabulary and concepts… igniting a sense of wonder.”
We aim for pupils to:
Ask thoughtful questions to deepen understanding
Make predictions using prior knowledge
Observe and measure accurately
Plan enquiries and record findings clearly
Interpret results and draw meaningful conclusions
Evaluate their own and others’ scientific ideas
We believe Science is not only knowledge, but also “the acquisition of concepts, skills and positive attitudes.” Every child’s scientific path is valued, cultivated and encouraged.
IMPLEMENTATION
Science is taught through Plymouth Science, our carefully selected scheme that ensures full National Curriculum coverage, clear progression and a strong balance of practical and written learning.
Key features of our implementation include:
Scientific Enquiry at the Heart
Children are regularly involved in practical investigations, fair testing and hands‑on exploration. They learn not just what happens, but why — developing reasoning skills and scientific thinking.
High‑Quality Teaching
Lessons begin with recapping prior learning and key vocabulary. New concepts are introduced through clear visual inputs (e.g., PowerPoints), teacher modelling and high‑quality questioning.
Practical & Written Balance
Plymouth Science provides structured units with opportunities for both practical enquiry and written outcomes, ensuring pupils can demonstrate understanding in multiple ways.
Cross‑Curricular Links
Science learning connects with:
Maths (calculating results, measuring)
Geography (area, environmental study)
Oracy (discussion, sharing findings)
Lesson Structure You Will See Across School
Quality first teaching adapted for all learners
Active, engaged pupils exploring scientific ideas
High‑quality questioning to deepen understanding
Recap of previous learning and vocabulary
Clear learning objective shared and revisited
Practical or written activity to apply knowledge
Plenary to consolidate new concepts
Adaptive Teaching & Inclusion
Our Science curriculum is fully adaptable to support SEND and disadvantaged pupils.
Adaptations include:
Pre‑teaching vocabulary
Scaffolded written tasks
Practical alternatives
Revisiting and consolidating learning
Non‑Negotiables
Correct scientific terminology used consistently
Front covers showing learning and concepts
Accessible, organised resources
Updated working walls
Scientific focus shared and referred to throughout
IMPACT
The impact of our Science curriculum is monitored through:
Our newly adapted assessment platform
By the end of KS2, pupils leave Churcham with:
A breadth of scientific knowledge
Confidence using scientific vocabulary
Strong enquiry skills
A positive attitude towards investigation
The ability to talk proudly and clearly about their learning
Why Science Matters at Churcham:
Science helps pupils:
Understand the world around them
Think critically and logically
Ask questions and seek answers
Work collaboratively
Build resilience through investigation
Develop confidence in explaining ideas

Curriculum
Our Curriculum at Churcham
Our Curriculum
At Churcham Primary School, our curriculum is designed to give every child the knowledge, skills and personal qualities they need to thrive — today, tomorrow and in the future. We want pupils to be curious, confident, resilient and proud of who they are. Our curriculum is ambitious for all, carefully sequenced, and rooted in our Christian values and ethos.
We recognise every child as a unique individual and celebrate the diversity within our school community. Our curriculum builds on pupils’ prior learning and provides rich, meaningful experiences that help them make sense of the world and develop a lifelong love of learning.
Our Curriculum Intent
Our curriculum aims to:
Teach the precise, essential knowledge pupils need to know and remember
Raise aspirations and broaden pupils’ understanding of what is possible
Provide purpose and relevance, connecting learning to real life
Develop character, resilience, independence and interpersonal skills
Ensure inclusion, so all pupils — including SEND and disadvantaged — can succeed
Promote curiosity, creativity and imagination
Prepare pupils for life, enabling them to make informed choices and flourish
Curriculum Implementation
Our curriculum is carefully planned and sequenced so that pupils build knowledge over time. Subject leaders ensure that:
Knowledge is broken down clearly, showing what pupils must learn and remember
Progression is mapped, so learning builds logically from EYFS to Year 6
Vocabulary is taught explicitly, supporting reading, writing and understanding
Retrieval practice helps pupils remember important knowledge long‑term
Assessment informs teaching, ensuring pupils keep up rather than catch up
Trips, visitors and real experiences enrich learning and deepen understanding
We use the National Curriculum as our foundation, adapting it to meet the needs of our pupils and our community.
Those who are more able are challenged to deepen and extend their learning. Pupils who need additional support receive targeted, evidence‑based interventions that help them embed key skills and progress at their own pace.
Curriculum Impact
By the time pupils leave Churcham, they:
Have secure knowledge across subjects
Can talk confidently about what they have learned and how it connects
Show resilience, independence and strong interpersonal skills
Demonstrate our Christian values in their actions and relationships
Feel a sense of belonging to a close, supportive community
Are ready for the next stage of their education as curious, capable, lifelong learners
Subject Leadership
Subject leaders play a vital role in ensuring our curriculum is effective. They:
Monitor teaching and learning
Review coverage, progression and impact
Support staff with subject knowledge
Evaluate strengths and areas for development
Ensure compliance with national and GCC expectations
This ongoing cycle of monitoring and review ensures our curriculum remains high‑quality, ambitious and responsive to pupils’ needs.
Find Out More
If you would like more information about our curriculum or individual subjects, please contact the school office. We are always happy to share how we design learning that helps every child shine.
